chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Mu'az narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and al-Fadl ibn Musa, who said: Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas.
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two blessings in which many people are tested are health and leisure.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two blessings in which most people are tested according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to illustrate the spiritual danger of complacency, where physical well-being and unoccupied time become tests of faith rather than opportunities for worship. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on active stewardship of one's faculties, warning that neglect leads to heedlessness (*ghaflah*) despite outward prosperity. The narration serves as a practical reminder to convert leisure into devotion and health into service, preventing the soul from falling into sin through ease.
